chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: Is it permissible that he touch a fox, a rabbit, or something from the beasts of prey, whether alive or dead? He said:
“It does not harm him, but he should wash his hand.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a disbeliever shakes hands with a Muslim while his hand is moist with sweat or something else, he washes it from his touch with water. If there is no moisture in it, he wipes it with some walls or dust.
That is indicated by His, Most High, saying:
So He judged them to be impure by the outward meaning of the wording; therefore, what they touch must be impure, except for what the shari'ah permits. This too indicates it.

key_terms.الثَّعْلَبَ: the fox, mentioned as an animal whose touch is being asked about
key_terms.السِّبَاعِ: beasts of prey, a category of wild animals referenced in the question
key_terms.الشَّرِيعَةُ: the sacred law, which specifies exceptions to the general ruling
key_terms.الْأَرْنَبَ: the rabbit, mentioned alongside other animals in the ruling
key_terms.رَطْبَةٌ: moist, indicating transfer of impurity in the discussed legal ruling
key_terms.نَجَسٌ: ritually impure, the Qur'anic term cited as proof
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ يَدَهُ: he should wash his hand, the practical ruling given in the report

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on touching wild animals or shaking hands with a disbeliever according to Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings of najasah and physical contact with certain animals, stating that touching them does not harm a person, though washing the hand is instructed. It also includes al-Shaykh’s legal discussion regarding contact with a disbeliever in the presence or absence of moisture, supported by the Qur'anic phrase about the impurity of the polytheists.
